svg.title: SupportPilot production system design
svg.desc: Clients, edge, stateless API tier, data tier, external services and observability, sized for 30,000 conversations per day.
svg.text: Target architecture for ≈30,000 support conversations/day (design point = 2× the busiest minute). Numbers from capacity/model.py; see docs/SCALING.md.
REST for turns · WebSocket for live
Redis hub fans events across pods
Stateless API Deployment · min 3 pods across 3 AZs · HPA: CPU + in-flight turns
ownership enforced server-side on every tool call
per-pod concurrency cap · queue timeout (20 s) · call timeout
overload ⇒ fallback model, else hand off to a human
KB index (BM25, in memory, reloaded on upload)
persona, branding, allowed origins, agent accounts
→ vector/hybrid index for very large KBs (roadmap)
drains ticket_outbox with exponential backoff (30 s → 1 h)
atomic claim (UPDATE … WHERE pending) · Jira idempotency
sync standby in 2nd AZ · PITR backups
pgvector or OpenSearch for large KBs
token secrets, agent keys, API keys
turn p95 < 12 s · error rate < 0.1 % · availability 99.9 %
model overload / timeout rate · outbox age & depth
authz violation ≥ 1 ⇒ page · handoff rate drift
audit_log: every order lookup and ticket
ship to SIEM; retention per privacy review
5 conv/s · ≈33 turns/s · ≈205 model calls in flight · ≈855 open chats

① widget loads from CDN → ② customer's backend mints user token; widget opens a session via WAF/LB → ③ pod verifies token, runs the orchestrator turn → ④ state persisted (Postgres) and events published (Redis) → ⑤ model / order / ticket calls as needed; reply returned and pushed to sockets on any pod.
Humans: handoff ⇒ conversation enters the Postgres-backed queue; agent console receives it live over WebSocket; claim is an atomic compare-and-set so only one agent wins.
